page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / Acting up
title: Acting up
topic: Language to use when you're in charge
description:
Last time at Tip Top Trading we heard Anna give the perfect elevator pitch for her new plastic aubergine idea to her boss. But Paul went off to a biscuit-lover's convention and hasn't come back! What's happened, and more importantly who will step up to take charge while the boss is missing?
This episode focuses on language that you might use when you have to 'act up' as the boss.
phrases: If anyone has any issues about their work please come and speak to me.
I would like to have a meeting to discuss our work.
If there is anything you want to ask, my door is always open.

listening_challenge.question: What does Denise want to do a bit more of, now that Anna is in charge?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Welcome back to English at Work. Last time we heard Anna pitching her new plastic aubergine idea to Paul, in a lift. He was on his way to a biscuit-lovers' convention and didn't have much time. She gave the perfect elevator pitch but it's down to Paul to give her idea the go ahead – the problem is, he seems to have gone missing.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Denise, isn't Paul supposed to be here today?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Yes. He went to that biscuit-lovers' convention yesterday but he said he'd be back today.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Maybe he's eloped with a pack of custard creams, eh?!

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Very funny Tom. I'll give him a call now …oh, that might be him now. Hello, Tip Top Trading… oh hello Paul, everything OK? ...oh no! ...oh no!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: What Denise?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: He choked on a biscuit at the convention and he's in hospital. (To Paul) Yes Paul, that was Tom… you want to speak to Anna? I'll just get her… get better soon Paul. (To Anna) Anna, Anna, it's Paul on the phone, he wants to speak to you – sounds important.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Me? Oh right, can you transfer the call please? Hello Paul, are you OK?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Not really. Damn Garibaldi biscuit got wedged in my throat, ended up banging my head on a table trying to get it out.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh dear, so you're not coming to work today?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: I'm afraid not, I need to rest for a few days so I was wondering, in fact I'm asking you, could you act up?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I've told you before Paul, I can't act… or even sing.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: No, no Anna. Act up, I mean do my job for a bit – be the boss – just for a day or two.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Me?! Be the boss?!

transcript.speaker: Tom/Denise
transcript.text: What?!

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: It's quite easy really. Just check my diary and you'll see what needs doing. And if you have any problems just… erm… just ask Denise. Thanks Anna.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: That's great Anna. You've got all the skills to do Paul's job – maybe even more! But you need to take charge and show who's boss!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh right. But what should I say?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Well, don't be too bossy, but you could say: "If anyone has any issues about their work please come and speak to me", or, "I would like to have a meeting to discuss our work", or, "If there's anything you want to ask, my door is always open". That makes you sound like a very approachable boss! Good luck.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text:
Thanks.
Right everyone, as you know Paul has put me in charge for a while.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: I'm not being funny Anna, but why you? I mean, I've been here the longest.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Tom, if you have any issues about your work, please come and speak to me.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Oh right… I will then.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Erm… Anna… congratulations on your promotion. I just wondered, now you're in charge, could I do a little less admin and a bit more selling?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Let's see Denise. I'd like to have a meeting soon to discuss all our work, so we can talk about it then. OK?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Oh yes, thanks Anna.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Right then. It's business as usual and if there's anything you want to ask, my door is always open. Right, back to work… and Tom, could I have a word in my office now please?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Excellent work Anna. You're sounding like the boss already – just don't start eating biscuits! Being in charge means being firm but fair and keeping your cool. Here's a reminder of some of the phrases Anna used:
If anyone has any issues about their work please come and speak to me.
I would like to have a meeting to discuss our work.
If there is anything you want to ask, my door is always open.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Take a seat Tom. Could you please close the door?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: I thought "your door was always open"?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Not this time. I need to speak to you about this message in Paul's diary.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Oh, right, I see. You need my help? What does it say?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: It's for two days' time and it says, Socrates, IPC, final.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Oh no, that doesn't sound good.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Oh dear, what could that mean? Could there be trouble ahead? Join us again soon to find out. Bye.
